ios.head: App Total Revenue +22.7% does not match new subs -0.8% from 7 days earlier — this growth is not coming from new customers.
ios.body: App Total Revenue on 11-05 vs 10-29 is +22.7%, but App Total New Subs on 10-29 vs 10-22 was -0.8% — they did not move together. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 11-05 vs 10-29): Subscription +23.6%, Pay as you go -3.8%. Since new subs barely moved while Subscription revenue (+23.6%) did not follow them, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

ios.head: Where installs come from is shifting toward Organic Install (+22.4% vs +15.5% for installs overall).
ios.body: Organic Install (YMK · US) was 1,180, +22.4% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved +15.5% — a difference of +6.8 percentage points. Organic Install is now 29.4% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

ios.head: YMK · US: Install change reads differently because the comparison average had 473 Unavailable installs.
ios.body: Only 3 Unavailable installs on the analysis day, but the comparison average had 473 (12%), so the % change depends on whether they are counted. Without them Install is 4,017 (+15.5% vs past-4-week avg); with them it would be 4,020 (+1.8%). Organic Install is +22.4% without them instead of -17.7%.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install -12.1% — Organic Install is behind most of it (-1,652, -14.7%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 21,079, against 23,968 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of -2,889. Where that came from: Organic Install -1,652 (-14.7%), Paid Install -1,042 (-9.7%), SEO Install -135 (-8.6%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (-1,652, -14.7%) and is now 45.3% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first. Known event: YCP iOS was delisted from the App Store on 2026-10-21 (因下架); its iOS Install / New User collapse is expected and its Install→New Subs conversion is an artefact. YCP accounts for about 100% of this change (-4,336).

insights.title: Market trend — YMK is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-13.9%, now 9.9%).
insights.body: In YMK, 9.9% of installs now turn into new subs — -13.9% versus last period. It is about 47% of revenue (a big revenue market): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in BR (-16.1%), while US grows (+19.9%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is BR -544 (-16.1%, about 3% of revenue); the biggest Subscription gain is US +5,384 (+19.9%); Pay as you go moved most in JP +1,425 (+124.9%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (43% of its revenue vs 6.5% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YMK is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-1.3% vs Install +9.1%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YMK New Subs -1.3% vs Install +9.1% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.
